visualReview.notes: Inspected all 11 current portable/source-terrain frames. Surviving Utrecht Domkerk has a broad north/south transept, central western gable/entry, narrow polygonal eastern choir, gray slate cross roof, lower ambulatory/chapels, pointed recessed glazing and restrained pale tracery. Warm gray-pink brick and stone, flying buttress curves, stepped piers and pinnacles carry the medium-fi identity. Separate Dom Tower remains west across an open square: broad square base with a real through-passage, narrower square belfry, open octagonal upper lantern, slate cap and metal tip. South U-shaped low cloister has open garden arcades and a clear central courtyard. Fixed a thin plan sliver that distorted the choir roof, separated low vestry/porch walls and roofs, regularized tiny outer buttress notches to the mapped high/aisle union, restored the central west gable and omitted an arcade blocked by the annex. Detailed foundation retains the raw mapped perimeter. Exact sculpture, clock/inscription detail, bells and internal stairs are omitted.
